name: Foundational Japanese (JLPT N5)
credits: Hand-curated against JLPT N5 specifications + Genki I + Tae Kim's Grammar Guide. Sequenced for first-150-minute pedagogical depth. Surface forms checked against JMdict headwords; kana-only entries (greetings, particles) use the kana form, kanji entries use the primary kanji.

levels.name: First Steps
levels.can_do: Greet, introduce yourself, ask and answer basic questions, count, tell time, talk about family, food, and simple daily activities. Read hiragana and katakana fluently and recognise ~100 kanji.

units.title: Greetings & politeness
units.goal: Greet at different times of day. Thank, apologise, accept/refuse.

vocab.surface: ありがとうございます

phrases.target: ありがとうございます。
すみません、わかりません。
お元気ですか? — はい、元気です。
phrases.en: How are you? — Yes, I'm well.

units.grammar_note: Politeness in Japanese is tier-based. ありがとう (casual) → ありがとうございます (polite). When unsure, use the longer form with strangers and elders.

units.title: Self introduction
units.goal: Give your name, nationality, ask someone's name.

phrases.target: 初めまして。私はアレックスです。
phrases.en: Nice to meet you. I'm Alex.

phrases.target: よろしくお願いします。
phrases.en: Pleased to meet you / I'm in your care.

units.grammar_note: 「〜は〜です」 (X wa Y desu) is the foundational sentence: 'X is Y'. は is the topic marker (pronounced 'wa', not 'ha').

units.title: Numbers & age
units.goal: Count 0-100, give your age.

phrases.target: 何歳ですか? — 三十歳です。

units.grammar_note: Japanese numbers are positional: 21 = 二十一 (ni-juu-ichi, two-ten-one). 'shi' for four is unlucky (homophone of death); 'yon' is safer in counts.

units.title: Days & time
units.goal: Name days of the week, today/tomorrow/yesterday, ask the time.

phrases.target: 今、何時ですか? — 三時です。
phrases.en: What time is it now? — It's 3 o'clock.

units.grammar_note: Days end in 曜日 (youbi = 'day-of-the-week'). The first character is the element: 月=moon (Mon), 火=fire (Tue), 水=water (Wed)... matches the planetary week.

units.title: Family
units.goal: Name immediate family using polite and humble forms.

phrases.target: あなたのお姉さんは何歳ですか?
phrases.en: How old is your older sister?

units.grammar_note: Two forms per relation: humble (talking about YOUR family — 父/母/兄) vs polite (talking about SOMEONE ELSE'S family — お父さん/お母さん/お兄さん).

units.title: Food, drink, ordering
units.goal: Name common foods, order at a restaurant, say what you like.
units.grammar_note: Particles: を marks the direct object (ご飯**を**食べる = eat rice), が marks the subject of likes (お茶**が**好き = like tea). Both look small but change the sentence's role completely.

units.title: Places & directions
units.goal: Name common places, say where you are, ask where things are.

phrases.en: The bookstore is in front of the school.

phrases.target: 猫は椅子の下にいます。
phrases.en: The cat is under the chair.

units.grammar_note: Location words come AFTER the place: X の前 (in front of X), X の下 (under X). Use いる for living things (cat is...), ある for non-living (book is...).

units.title: Daily activities
units.goal: Describe a daily routine using core verbs.

phrases.target: 毎日、日本語を勉強します。

units.grammar_note: Polite present/future verb: drop る (for ichidan verbs like 食べる, 見る) and add ます: 食べる → 食べます (eat / will eat).

units.title: School & learning
units.goal: Talk about studying Japanese, classroom objects, books.

phrases.target: 日本語を勉強しています。

units.grammar_note: Japanese uses three writing systems together: hiragana (ひらがな) for grammar/native words, katakana (カタカナ) for foreign loans, kanji (漢字) for content roots.

units.title: Body & feelings
units.goal: Name body parts, say how you feel, what hurts.
units.grammar_note: Pain pattern: 〜が痛い (X ga itai = X hurts). Body part + が + 痛い: 頭が痛い (head hurts), 歯が痛い (tooth hurts).

units.title: Weather & seasons
units.goal: Describe the weather, name seasons.
units.grammar_note: Weather verbs use 降る (furu = to fall) for precipitation: 雨が降る (rain falls), 雪が降る (snow falls).

units.title: Shopping & money
units.goal: Ask prices, shop, describe items as big/small/cheap/expensive.

phrases.target: もう少し安いのはありますか?
phrases.en: Do you have something a bit cheaper?

units.grammar_note: Demonstratives form three groups: こ-words (near speaker: これ this), そ-words (near listener: それ that), あ-words (far: あれ over there).

levels.name: Everyday Fluency
levels.can_do: Talk about past events, ongoing actions, plans, and feelings. Switch between plain and polite registers. Make requests, give permission, describe people and places with adjective conjugation. Read short narrative paragraphs and recognise ~300 kanji.

units.title: Past tense — polite & plain
units.goal: Describe what happened yesterday / last week using ました and た-form.

phrases.target: 昨日、友達に会いました。
もう宿題をしましたか? — いいえ、まだです。
phrases.en: Did you do your homework yet? — No, not yet.
I went to Tokyo last week. (plain)

phrases.target: 電話をくれてありがとう。
テストが終わりました。

units.grammar_note: Polite past: ます → ました (食べました = ate), です → でした (静かでした = was quiet). Plain past = た-form: 食べる → 食べた, 行く → 行った, ある → あった.

units.title: Te-form & ongoing actions
units.goal: Connect clauses and express ongoing/resultant states with ている.

phrases.target: 今、ご飯を食べています。
彼は東京に住んでいます。
私は田中さんを知っています。
公園で子供たちが遊んでいる。
phrases.en: The children are playing in the park. (plain)

phrases.target: 急いで歩いてください。

units.grammar_note: Te-form connects clauses and forms the progressive 〜ている. Godan rules: う/つ/る→って, む/ぶ/ぬ→んで, く→いて, ぐ→いで, す→して. Ichidan: drop る + て. Irregular: 行く→行って, する→して, 来る→来て.

units.title: Plain form (informal speech)
units.goal: Speak in plain/dictionary form with friends and family.
units.grammar_note: Plain form is the dictionary form. です→だ (or dropped after い-adj), ます-verbs go back to dictionary form. Use with close friends/family; using plain form with strangers can sound rude.

units.title: Negative forms
units.goal: Negate verbs, adjectives, and the copula in polite and plain registers.

vocab.gloss: is not (animate, plain neg of いる)

units.grammar_note: Plain neg: godan う→わ + ない (買う→買わない), ichidan drop る + ない (食べる→食べない). Irregulars: ある→ない, する→しない, 来る→来ない. Past neg: なかった. ない conjugates like an i-adjective.

units.title: Adjective conjugation — i & na
units.goal: Conjugate i-adjectives and na-adjectives for past, negative, and connective forms.

phrases.target: この町は静かで便利です。
phrases.en: This town is quiet and convenient.

phrases.target: 昨日のテストは難しかった。
あの店は有名じゃありません。
ラーメンは熱くて辛かったです。
phrases.en: The ramen was hot and spicy.
My mother is skilled at cooking.

units.grammar_note: i-adj past: い→かった (高い→高かった). Neg: い→くない (高くない). Connective: い→くて (高くて). na-adj uses copula: 静かでした (was quiet), 静かじゃない (isn't quiet), 静かで (and quiet,...).

units.title: Family & social — deepening
units.goal: Describe relationships, social events, and people's traits.

phrases.target: 今度の土曜日、誕生日のパーティーをします。
phrases.en: We're having a birthday party this Saturday.
My husband is a quiet person.

phrases.target: 友達を紹介してもいいですか?
隣の家に新しい家族が来た。
phrases.en: A new family came to the house next door.

phrases.target: プレゼントをありがとう!

units.grammar_note: Family pairs follow N5's humble/polite split. 夫/妻 (my own) vs ご主人/奥さん (someone else's). Names take さん in conversation regardless of family — 田中さんの奥さん = Tanaka's wife.

units.title: Travel & transportation
units.goal: Book travel, name transport, describe a trip.

phrases.target: 新幹線で京都まで行きます。
phrases.en: I'll go to Kyoto by bullet train.

phrases.target: 切符を二枚予約しました。

phrases.en: I'll get off at the next station.

phrases.target: ホテルは駅の近くです。
phrases.en: The hotel is near the station.

phrases.target: 空港まで何分かかりますか?
phrases.en: How many minutes does it take to the airport?

units.grammar_note: Means of transport: で (by). 電車で = by train. Destination: に or へ. Source: から. Time required: 〜時間/分かかる. 乗る takes に (バスに乗る), but 降りる takes を (バスを降りる).

units.title: Work & school routines
units.goal: Describe a workday or school schedule, meetings, deadlines.

phrases.target: 明日の会議は十時からです。
発表の準備をしています。

phrases.en: I'm going to Osaka for a business trip. (plain)

units.grammar_note: Workplace verbs commonly use 〜する: 会議する (have a meeting), 残業する (work overtime), 出張する (go on a business trip). The noun and verb sense are the same root.

units.title: Health & emergencies
units.goal: Describe symptoms, ask for help, navigate a clinic visit.

phrases.target: 頭が痛くて、熱があります。
phrases.en: My head hurts and I have a fever.

phrases.target: 大丈夫ですか? — 大丈夫です。
気をつけて運転してください。

units.grammar_note: Symptom pattern: 〜が + 痛い (X hurts) or 〜があります (have X). 熱があります = I have a fever. Take medicine = 薬を飲む (literally 'drink medicine' — never 食べる).

units.title: Asking favors & requests
units.goal: Politely ask someone to do something; ask and grant permission.

phrases.target: ちょっと手伝ってください。
phrases.en: Please help me for a moment.

phrases.target: もう一度言ってください。
ここに座ってもいいですか? — はい、どうぞ。
phrases.en: May I sit here? — Yes, please.

phrases.target: 写真を撮ってもいいですか?
ここでタバコを吸ってはいけません。
辞書を貸してくれませんか?
phrases.en: Could you lend me a dictionary?

units.grammar_note: Request: 〜てください (please do). Permission: 〜てもいいですか (may I?). Prohibition: 〜てはいけません (must not). Softer request: 〜てくれませんか (could you...?).
